name: Bank Telemarketing Term Deposit
tagline: Predict term-deposit subscriptions with semicolon CSV parsing and call-duration leakage.
description:
Collected from direct outbound phone-call marketing campaigns of a Portuguese retail banking institution between May 2008 and November 2010 and published by Moro, Cortez, and Rita (2014), this canonical 45,211-record ('bank-full.csv') dataset predicts whether a contacted client subscribes to a long-term bank deposit ('y' = 'yes' in 11.7% of calls).

Bank Marketing serves four indispensable functions in Phase 1: (1) testing semicolon-delimited (';') CSV parsing in the browser; (2) illustrating post-outcome target leakage via 'duration' (call length in seconds is unknown before dialing and strongly reveals whether a sale occurred); (3) demonstrating severe 1:7.55 class imbalance where naive accuracy reaches 88.3% while predicting zero subscribers; and (4) auditing U-shaped age-group targeting disparities (25.6% subscription under age 25 and 42.3% over age 60 vs. 10.6% aged 25-60).

targetCandidates.description: Predict whether the contacted client subscribes to a bank term deposit ('yes' vs. 'no') using only pre-call attributes.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Client age in years (exhibits U-shaped conversion rates: higher among youth <25 and retirees >60 than working-age adults 25-60).

columns.name: job
columns.description: Client occupation category ('unknown' in 288 records represents unrecorded job status).

columns.name: marital
columns.description: Client marital status ('married', 'single', or 'divorced' [which includes widowed]).

columns.name: education
columns.description: Highest formal educational tier ('primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', or 'unknown' in 1,857 records).

columns.name: default
columns.description: Whether the client currently has credit in default.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Average yearly bank account balance in euros (can be negative when overdrawn).

columns.name: housing
columns.description: Whether the client holds an active residential mortgage loan.

columns.name: loan
columns.description: Whether the client holds an active personal consumer loan.

columns.name: contact
columns.description: Telecommunication channel used ('cellular', 'telephone', or 'unknown' in 13,020 records).

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day of the month (1 to 31) of the last campaign contact.

columns.name: month
columns.description: Calendar month abbreviation ('jan' through 'dec') of the last campaign contact.

columns.name: duration
columns.description: Duration of the last phone call in seconds; unknown prior to placing a call and strongly reveals whether the client stayed on the line to subscribe.
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome target leakage: call duration is unknown before placing a call and directly reflects enrollment completion (Moro et al., 2014).

columns.name: campaign
columns.description: Number of phone contacts performed during this campaign for this client (includes last contact).

columns.name: pdays
columns.description: Days elapsed since the client was last contacted in a prior campaign (-1 in 36,954 records indicates the client was never previously contacted).

columns.name: previous
columns.description: Number of contacts performed before the current marketing campaign for this client.

columns.name: poutcome
columns.description: Outcome of the prior marketing campaign ('success', 'failure', 'other', or 'unknown' for the 36,959 uncontacted/unrecorded cases).

columns.name: y
columns.description: Whether the client subscribed to the offered bank term deposit.

references.title: A Data-Driven Approach to Predict the Success of Bank Telemarketing

warnings: Variant Ambiguity Warning (Simson et al., 2025): UCI distributes four Bank Marketing files (45,211x17 'bank-full.csv' used here, 4,521x17 'bank.csv', 41,188x21 'bank-additional-full.csv', and 4,119x21 'bank-additional.csv'); never compare metrics across papers without verifying which variant and whether leaky 'duration' were used.

Automated financial product targeting disproportionately selects older retirees (>60) and excludes working-age adults (25-60), raising dual ethical questions around exclusionary financial marketing vs. predatory telemarketing of seniors.
